event.title: Tropical Storm Bertha Approaches Gulf Coast as Hurricane Fausto Develops in Eastern Pacific
event.canonical_title: Tropical Storm Bertha Approaches Gulf Coast as Hurricane Fausto Develops in Eastern Pacific
event.summary: Tropical Storm Bertha has formed in the Gulf of Mexico and is moving toward the Gulf Coast, posing risks of heavy rain, storm surge, and damaging winds. Meanwhile, Hurricane Fausto has developed in the eastern Pacific Ocean, although it is located far from populated areas. Preparations are underway in coastal regions as Bertha approaches.

timeline.title: Tropical Storm Bertha Approaches Gulf Coast, Prompting Beach Closures and Flood Preparations
timeline.summary: Tropical Storm Bertha is approaching the Gulf Coast, leading to beach closures and the filling of sandbags in preparation for heavy rain and potential flooding. This storm follows Tropical Storm Arthur, which recently caused significant flooding in the region.
key_facts: Tropical Storm Bertha is the second storm of the Atlantic hurricane season.
Coastal areas are preparing for heavy rain and flooding.

timeline.title: Tropical Storm Bertha Makes Landfall in Southern Louisiana
timeline.summary: Tropical Storm Bertha made landfall on southern Louisiana, approximately 40 miles east of New Orleans, bringing strong winds and prompting beach closures from the Florida Panhandle to Mississippi. The storm is now moving toward Texas as it continues to weaken.

event_overview.title: About Tropical Storms
event_overview.subject: Tropical Storms
event_overview.summary: This tracked event concerns concurrent tropical cyclones affecting two U.S. National Hurricane Center monitoring areas: Bertha in the Atlantic basin, including the Gulf Coast, and Fausto in the eastern North Pacific. Tropical storms are named tropical cyclones with sustained winds of 39–73 mph; once sustained winds reach 74 mph, they are classified as hurricanes.

facts.label: Seasonal timing
facts.value: The Atlantic hurricane season, which includes the Gulf of America, officially runs from June 1 through November 30; the eastern Pacific season runs from May 15 through November 30.

facts.label: Geographic scope
facts.value: The eastern North Pacific basin is the portion of the North Pacific Ocean east of 140°W, while the Atlantic basin includes the Atlantic Ocean, Caribbean Sea, and Gulf of America.

facts.label: Storm classifications
facts.value: A tropical storm has maximum sustained winds of 39–73 mph; a hurricane has maximum sustained winds of at least 74 mph. Major hurricanes are Category 3–5 systems, beginning at 111 mph.

facts.label: Forecasting authority
facts.value: NOAA’s National Hurricane Center in Miami is responsible for tracking tropical cyclones in both the Atlantic and eastern North Pacific and issues operational products including forecasts, public advisories, discussions, and wind-probability information for active cyclones.

facts.label: Naming system
facts.value: Bertha is on the 2026 Atlantic storm-name list. Tropical-cyclone names are assigned from rotating lists maintained through the World Meteorological Organization system.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline follows the July 21–23, 2026 developments involving Bertha’s approach and reported landfall and Fausto’s concurrent eastern-Pacific development; it does not attempt to provide a complete storm lifecycle, full warning record, or final damage and casualty assessment.
